I believe that I heard Siljkovici. That was the name of the village. So maybe this could be clarified. Sekovici is on the completely different side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you can say that Sekovici is a village. Yes. I think you need to clarify this with the witness. I think he must have said Siljkovici, which is opposite Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll clarify that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, a few moments ago you testified that your group was moving in the area of Kravica and another town. Do you recall what the other town was? And the transcript indicates that it was Sekovici. Pardon my pronunciation. I don't know if there was another town that you had in mind other than that described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not even a town, actually. If it's Siljkovici, it's not a town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were moving towards Konjevic Polje, and we got to the village of Kamenica, which belongs to the Bratunac municipality. Siljkovici and Kravica are below Kamenica. What I said was that people were fleeing towards Kravica and Siljkovici, not Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I thank you, Mr. Lazarevic, as well. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Thayer. And when he said that they entered, or when they arrived sometime in the evening at the village of Kamenica, that's page 46, line 11, 10 and 11, that he actually means they entered the village of Kamenica or they arrived nearby the village, near the village of Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, near the village of Kamenica, nearby. In fact, it's a forest near Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that explains it as well. Sorry for interrupting you, Mr. Thayer, but I think this needed clarification. You may proceed. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, up until the ambush which occurred in the area of Kamenica, which relatives do you recall being with you at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Some of my cousins were with me, and then our neighbours. I ran into some neighbours, and I asked them where my father was, and I headed towards him and then the shooting broke out, and that's where I lost track of my father, and I still haven't been able to find him. I couldn't find him among the dead, among the wounded. He was not there. Therefore, I lost any track of him since that point, and no one ever saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, following this ambush at Kamenica, can you describe what you and the members of your group did following the attack.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We gathered on a meadow, and we agreed to go back to get -- to fetch the wounded, to get them to the meadow, and that's what we did. We took them out on the -- in the meadow. And someone was negotiating with the Chetniks, with the Serbs, to let us continue on our path, and it seems that they said that the wounded should go first. That's why we recovered the wounded, and we set off across a meadow. When we got to the middle of the meadow, we were fired upon from all the sides, and at that point we were forced to leave the wounded and to flee, because we were out in the open in the meadow. And I in fact ended up in a river. I drank some water there, and then we continued to a port. I was able to get -- to reach a forest. There were -- there was a group of us, and we went uphill. We didn't know where we were heading. And we went to an opening. There were about 300 people sitting there, on the hill. We left the wounded behind. Many people were killed on the meadow, the people who were trying to carry the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you met up with this group of approximately 300 people, do you have any specific idea of where you were at the time or just a general idea of where you were at the time, sir? And can you describe where you believe that place was.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I didn't know where I was. There was this hill, there was this opening, there was this -- on the hill. And when I came there, I met up with Alija and my cousin Esref, and I asked them if they had seen anybody else from the village. They said that they didn't. And at that time, someone appeared, with a moustache, who said that he could lead us out of there, because nobody knew where to go. And then he came out -- he came there and he said that he would lead us. I was a bit suspicious because I had never seen him before. Srebrenica is a small town, and I had never seen him, neither as a military man nor as a civilian, so I didn't really trust him. I think that this was a Chetnik, actually, who was infiltrated, because in Kamenica, during the ambush, they were infiltrated into our group, and they claimed to be of our group. So I didn't trust him, and I told him that he should stay at the end of the column. And then we headed down the meadow, down the hill. We came near the river. There was a river down there. When we came to the river, we gathered there, and at that point this man disappeared. I didn't see him after that. And they told us, "Don't run away - surrender." And then they started shooting. They started shooting with the artillery weapons, with the anti-aircraft guns. There was chaos. And at that point I started running down the meadow. I ran to a forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me stop you right there, sir. When you say that someone said, "Don't run away - surrender," who do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The Chetniks who were along the path, who were controlling this path from -- to Bratunac. They told us to surrender, not to run away, and they were firing upon us.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you just testified that you described this path as running to Bratunac, sir. What direction do you recall you were heading in? Towards what town were you heading, sir, at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We were heading towards Konjevic Polje, so that this road was always to our right side, this road to Bratunac. It was always on our right side. I don't recall the exact spot where the river was because it was night.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified a moment ago that after the most recent attack that you described where Serbs, to your recollection, said, "Don't run away - surrender," you started running down the meadow and to a forest. Could you please describe for the Trial Chamber what happened after that point, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I ran uphill. I came to a forest. I was exhausted, tired. Birch tree, and I sat down -- I lay down. I couldn't stand any more. I went to sleep. There was no one around. And when I woke up, there was a road next to me. I couldn't see it during night. And then a column of people came up to where I was standing. They were civilians with backpacks, and I recognised that these were people from Srebrenica. I recognised also some people from Slatina. There was also Bajro Oric, a cousin of mine. I approached them. And there was also another person who lived in Jela, above Konjevic Polje, who said that he knew where we should go. So I went with them. We went in the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just stop you right there, sir. When you awoke, this would have been sometime on 13 July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That is correct. On the 13th of July, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just so I have it clear in my head, you described waking up next to a road. Can you describe that road?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It was a dirt road, a village path, overgrown and bushes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In other words, sir, it wasn't the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road that you were roughly following the previous day. Is that -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No. No. As I said, this was a dirt road on -- across the mountains, which connected villages. It was not a regular road towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this group of people with whom you met up, do you recall approximately how many people were in it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We were 13 in this group. And then we went to Selo -- to the village Jela to have some water, to have some fruits. We found a cherry tree. We ate some cherries and we had some water. This -- the person I mentioned lived in this village, the one who was leading us. We rested there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did this group that you were travelling with try to do? Where were you trying to head at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We were above Konjevic Polje, and we wanted to go -- to take the road Konjevic Polje-Milici-Nova Kasaba. We went near the road and they fired at us, we went back, and we spent the whole day there, somewhere near Konjevic Polje. We spent the whole day there. We were fired at by shells. They -- they asked from us to surrender, and in the evening, around 9.00, we decided -- around 7.00, we decided to head towards Konjevic Polje. I think it was 7.30. We headed towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just stop you right there, sir, again. You described being above Konjevic Polje. Were you situated on a hill, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And from that vantage point were you able to see the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje portion of that paved road?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We were able to see the road. We also saw the tanks and Pragas firing at us, and the UNPROFOR carrier. We were able to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you just referred to an UNPROFOR carrier. What makes you believe that that was an UNPROFOR carrier, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It was white. It had "UN" written on it, and the Serbs were asking from us to surrender. We were told that nothing would happen to us. And a number of them went to surrender, believing that UNPROFOR was there, that they were safe, that they wouldn't be hurt. They were calling through a loudspeaker.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You testified that later on that day, towards evening, I believe you said it was about 7.00 or 7.30, you moved closer to the road, that Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what happened next, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No. We set off around 7.30. We took a small path towards the paved road to come nearer to the road, and to wait there till night falls to be able to -- to take this road in the night-time when they're asleep. But when we came halfway near a torched house, we -- some people came from the back and they told us not to move and to raise our hands. We turned around. They were Chetniks, the same ones who told us not to run away, although we couldn't run away because we had nowhere to run away to. That's why we stopped. We surrendered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: These people that stopped you, were they Serb soldiers, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, they had automatic rifles and an 84, M-84 machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at the time that you encountered these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whether they were wearing any uniforms, please, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, were these Serb soldiers wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe them? If you can, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They had camouflage uniforms, boots. They had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And with these soldiers, at the time were you able to notice any particular insignia, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: At that moment, we didn't have any time. They told us to lie down on our stomachs and to put our hands behind our heads, and that's how we stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did these soldiers search you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At that time, how many people were in your group?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: There were nine of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You had previously described approximately a dozen people being in your group. Do you recall what happened to the -- to the others?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Three went to reconnoiter and never returned in the course of that day. They went to see whether we could go somewhere else, whether we could take another path, but they never returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you happen to recognise any of the soldiers who captured you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I recognised one, and he recognised me as well. That was a neighbour of mine from Studenac. I didn't know his name. I believe that his family name was either Gligic or Simic. He recognised me when we stood up and he asked me where I had served the JNA. I told him I was in Gnjilane. Then he cursed me, and then he told me to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, this -- this soldier whose name you recall as being either Gligic or Simic, based on your relationship with him, did he know that you had served elsewhere other than Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. He knew that I had gone to Croatia, that I was in HV for a while, and he knew that I had also served in my own army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did he also know that you were related to Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: He knew that my name was Oric and that Bajro's name was also Oric, but at that moment he didn't say anything to anybody. He didn't mention that fact to anybody, that our family name was Oric. And I believe that he helped us by not doing that. I believe that the others would have killed us there and then if he had ever mentioned that we were Naser Oric's relatives. I believe that he helped us by not saying who we are, and that's how we actually remained alive, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What did these soldiers do with you next, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They took us to Konjevic Polje, to a storage. Before the war this was an agricultural facility where the agriculture produce was bought from the farmers. We were put there in a room, and we were guarded by one guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to describe this as -- you refer to as a storage. Would it be fair to describe it as a warehouse, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, you may call it that. A storage, a warehouse with various rooms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Thayer. One of your questions was whether these Serb soldiers searched him and the others, and his answer was yes. Earlier on, he told us that he was carrying two hand grenades. Was he still carrying these two hand grenades? Were they found on his body? Perhaps you can address this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's coming down the line, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I apologise to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll ask it now. Actually, if I may just ask a couple of preliminary questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, go ahead, go ahead. I just wanted to draw your attention to it, that's all. When you ask the question is your business then.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, how were you treated when you arrived at this warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The guard treated us fairly. We spoke to him, and that moment as we were sitting down and the guard was there, an officer came. His shirt was unbuttoned. He was neatly shaved. He entered and asked us where our rifles were, and we told him that we did not have any rifles and we had never had any, and then he said, "Go back and fetch the rifles where you left them," and we told him we didn't have any and there was nothing to be brought back. Later on, one of the soldiers brought us water, cigarettes, beer, and there you have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just stop you right there. You told the officer that you had no rifles. You testified earlier that you had left Susnjari with two hand grenades. Do you know what became of those two hand grenades, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The two grenades, I lost them. They fell out of my pockets in Kamenica near an ambush. As I was crawling, looking for shelter, they came loose from my belt where I had them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So by the time your group of nine was captured, to your knowledge were any of you armed at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The officer who you described having the unbuttoned shirt who asked you about the rifles, did he tell you what was going to happen to you next?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: One of us asked him. I don't know who did. We asked him what would happen to us, and he answered that his duty was to capture us, to put us on buses and send us to Bratunac, and this is what transpired.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you also told that you would have to wait for anything?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: He told us to wait for the buses transporting civilians from Potocari to Kladanj, and when they returned the same buses would transport us to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did buses finally arrive?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Indeed they did. Two buses arrived from the direction of Milici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, perhaps I could ask your witness whether to his knowledge he and maybe any of the other eight were carrying any identification documents or documents which would identify them at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you understand that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, nobody had anything. Everything we had had been taken away from us in the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, when you say everything had been taken away from you in the forest, do you mean to say that you lost everything or that it was taken from you at the time of your capture?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: When we were captured everything was taken away from us. Mind you, I did not have anything on my body. I don't know about the others. Nobody had anything major. Maybe some had a pack of cigarettes and a lighter. That was all we had. Most people had thrown their documents even before that. Actually, I never took my documents from home because I had set out for Tuzla straight from the line. I never went home before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified that two buses finally arrived. Do you recall approximately what time of day on the 13th this was?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It was already late and the lights were on. For example, the headlights on the buses were on. It may have been around 9.00, 9.30, 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall which bus you boarded?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We boarded the first bus through the back door, and we sat on the last row of seats, and the three military policemen who guarded us on the bus went through the front door.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "we," are you referring to the group of nine with whom you were captured?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Trial Chamber exactly where on this first bus you were seated.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We occupied the back row of seats. As far as I know, these seats were referred to by a particular name, a settee, the last row of seats on any bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was there anything special about that back seat, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They were somewhat higher than the rest of the seats, so you had a good view of the entire interior of the bus. And the window is almost at the level of the seats, and you had a good view outside the bus if you were sitting on those seats, because they are elevated, higher than the rest of the seats on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you seated on the right-hand side or the left-hand side of the bus, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, next to the window. Actually, I was the first on the right-hand side, right next to the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You referred a moment ago to some military policemen boarding the bus with you. How many of these military policemen do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: There were three.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how do you know they were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Thayer. Sorry to interrupt you, but perhaps he could explain to us how he could distinguish military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That was my next question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We seem to be telepathic today.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm one step behind, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how do you know that these men were military policemen, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Because they had patches on their arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did these patches say that you recall?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: VP.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what does that stand for, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were these military policemen wearing anything else that you recall in particular, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I remember that they wore blue flak jackets as normally worn by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And had you become familiar with that style of flak jacket, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I was familiar with that type of uniform because I had used to see them every day on UNPROFOR soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe the appearance of those blue flak jackets, please.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No sleeves, blue down to the belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, last week, sir, I showed you a picture and -- which you've seen before. I'd like to show it to you again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I would ask that a video still be shown on e-court. The ERN is 01264884-0216-4884. It does not have a 65 ter number, I afraid, but we'll identify it by the ERN.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see an image on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Does anyone see an image in front of them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we don't have anything as yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the e-court isn't telepathic. And, Your Honour, if worst comes to worst, Mr. President, we can certainly placed it on the ELMO and do it the old-fashioned way. May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead. I think everyone has it on the screen, on their respective screens now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a image on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what, if anything in particular, does that picture show you that you recall?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: This depicts some soldiers and the bullet-proof vests that I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you stated that there's some soldiers. How many soldiers are in the picture, sir, that you can see? And if you need to refer to the original, which is on the ELMO, for better focus, please -- please do so, but how many soldiers do you see in the image?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I can see three soldiers and a fourth one whose back I can see. His back is turned toward these three soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's fair to say there are three soldiers in the foreground of the picture; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And which soldier is wearing the vest; the one on the left, right, or in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The one in the middle. He is wearing the UNPROFOR bullet-proof vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, the colour isn't coming through too well on our monitor, but can you see, either on your screen or on the original on the ELMO, what colour that vest is?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And does this picture fairly and accurately portray the UNPROFOR flak jackets that you recall the Serb soldiers wearing at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, moving on, sir. Did the buses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I may take this opportunity - I don't think it will interrupt the testimony - but this particular picture that we are seeing, that we are being shown is an example of the difficulties encountered by the Defence with the Rule 65 ter list of exhibits. In the particular list that we've been provided with, we had an Exhibit Number 1943, but there was no ERN number. When we were given the list of exhibits that were going to be used with the witness, we were told that there was an Exhibit 1943, but there was no exhibit number. We looked -- we go back to the list of exhibits, the Rule 65 ter list, and there's no ERN, but there is an ERN provided for a video. So we know what we were put on notice of before the testimony of this witness is that somewhere there's a still of three soldiers that will be shown that comes from a very long video. Now, given the description of this particular picture, he said a still of three soldier, we don't know why he's going to show it to the witness, and there's no way for us to prepare accordingly. Now we know that what he wanted to show was the blue flak jacket. But that's just to provide an example of the difficulties we face. And when I mentioned earlier on in this trial that when the Prosecution puts a still of a video on its list of exhibits, it has a purpose. The Prosecution wants to show a specific picture. And right now it's not possible for us to know what are these specific pictures that he wants to show with each witness. And I believe maybe a remedy for this in the meantime is that if they want to show a still and they give us, in their list of exhibits to be used with each witness, that they provide to us the exact picture they want to show, so at least we know in advance when the witness comes. Because in this case we did not know other than three soldiers. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you're right. At least, I speak in relation to what information that we were given, which also refers to a document -- one of the documents to be used as 1943 and described as a video still. At least in what we have it indicates of a Serb soldier, there is his name, and a Dutch soldier, and there is his name. So that also may have made it even more confusing. I think Mr. Bourgon's point is -- needs to be well taken, and I'm sure that in the future there will be a better approach or a more systematic and more usefully indicative approach to this, because it can be confusing. I hundred per cent agree with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we recognise that can be confusing. In this case, and what our practice has been pursuant to the Court's order in terms of disclosing the exhibits we intend to use with a particular witness, this ERN was provided. It is the ERN on the document, and it is readily obtainable via the ERN. This has been, to our understanding, available for almost two weeks now since we disclosed this list -- well, in any event, Your Honour, it came in through e-court, as I understand it, and it has been made available. We will continue to try our best to be as specific as possible in describing the exhibits, obviously. This has a little bit of a shortcoming in terms of describing precisely what's in the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Definitely it is. And while we are at it, since at least the document that we have says video still of Serb soldier and Dutch soldier, you could perhaps explain whether this is correct or not and who would be the Serb soldier in this picture, whether he's the one wearing the blue flak jacket, because if that is the case, then you need to address the other matter that, according to the witness, these flak jackets were worn by UNPROFOR soldiers. It doesn't seem that any of the UNPROFOR soldiers are wearing that flak jacket here. So this is why I -- I think Mr. Bourgon is hundred per cent right. I don't know -- I wouldn't know who is the Serb soldier in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- this witness has been called for the purpose of simply identifying the type of vest that he recalls seeing some of the Serb soldiers wearing. So it wasn't my intention to -- for him to identify whether this particular individual was a Serb or another was a Dutch soldier. I believe that level of testimony will come out through subsequent witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, again, Your Honour, this particular document has been made known to the Defence with great specificity through this ERN, which is on the exhibit list for this witness and is listed on this document. This also is very specifically described in prior testimony in Blagojevic, and it was released in e-court as Thursday of last week, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, let's forget excuses and justifications. Just saying that, at least to us, this is very misleading, and if we were Defence counsel, I would -- the whole idea of having this is not to have to go through an entire exercise of identifying from the previous list which one would be this video still, because this is the whole -- the whole -- the whole exercise is meant to facilitate the whole exercise and not to make it complicated. So let's -- you've got the message. You've also heard us say that we believe that Mr. Bourgon's point is -- should be well taken, and we take it up from there, and we try to be more specific in the future, that's all. In the meantime, let's move forward, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I hear the message loud and clear, Your Honour, and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, did the buses eventually leave Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. We headed towards Bratunac. The road to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was your bus still the first bus in line?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you make any stops on the way?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We stopped in Kravica. They opened the front and the rear doors, and -- and prisoners were loaded, or they entered. They came in. They were, in fact, situated on a meadow near the road. So they boarded the bus, the buses, with prisoners, and then we continued towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you described a meadow in Kravica. Was that meadow located near any structure in particular that you recall, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: There is a facility like a warehouse, and the prisoners were sitting next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you estimate for the Trial Chamber approximately how many prisoners you observed in this meadow.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: As far as I could see from the bus, according to my assessment, 400 to 500 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that some of those prisoners were placed on your two buses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was my bus and another bus, and the prisoners were placed on the bus, and the bus was full with people.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, the prisoners that you observed in the meadow, were they guarded by anyone?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: There were soldiers around the bus -- around the buses, guarding them. There were soldiers around.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were there soldiers located in the meadow as well, guarding those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that we're approaching the next break. I've no more questions on this particular topic and am prepared to move on to the next topic after the break, if that suits the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly, Mr. Thayer. We'll have a 20-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you. Two brief preliminary matters, if I could. I don't want to take too much time since we have the witness sitting here. The first is I just wanted to advise the Court that we have met with Defence counsel during the break in an effort to really try to avoid further confusion with regard to disclosure and documents and e-court and that whole process. We'll continue to do that. We've really tried to have a meeting of the minds as to how to best utilise and make sure we're doing this properly and that Defence counsel has access to, as we thought they did, to everything on e-court well in advance of the witness's testimony, and we'll pledge to continue to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I never had any doubt about that, neither in this case nor in any other case that I've been involved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Secondly, Your Honour, at your suggestion I've identified two maps that I'm prepared to examine Mr. Oric with, if the Court pleases. This is as good a time as any to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I tried to advise as many Defence counsel as I could during the break, but for those who missed it, I'll be showing Mr. Oric map 6. Actually I think I'd mentioned map 5 before, but map 6 is a slight magnification of the section of map 5 that I'd been thinking about. The other map is attached to Mr. Oric's August 10th through 12th, 1995, OTP witness interview. I believe it is the very last document of the exhibits attached to his statement. He has some sketches, and I believe the last document is this map. And I'm sorry that we don't have enough copies in hard copy to distribute, but I can certainly put it on the ELMO and everybody should be able to see. This map is -- has an ERN, not a court identification number, and I understand my use of the ERN number before it may have caused some confusion. I apologise if I contributed to that confusion. But this has an old-fashioned ERN of 00337000, just for the sake of the record. With that, Your Honour, I believe I'm prepared to proceed to do my best with these maps, and Mr. Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if I may hand a map to you, and I know that we've not had an opportunity to look at this previously, but I'd ask you to take a look at this map which we'll place on the ELMO. And please, just take a moment to review it and orient yourself to the map and just let us know when -- when you're ready to proceed, when you feel comfortable identifying places on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just want to make this clear: We are not using e-court now, are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So if he's going to put marks, to mark that map, is that a spare copy that you are using there that can then be signed by him and entered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's an extra copy we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure. And you are all comfortable with this on the Defence side? Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, have you had an opportunity to look at the map and do you feel comfortable discussing in general locations and events which occurred in the area depicted by this map?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I have never seen this map before, but we can try. I can see that only Jaglici and Konjevic Polje are indicated. Kamenica, where the ambush occurred, is not on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is why I said if you get a survey map it would be much, much better. There are excellent survey maps of this area which I have used in other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have a second map that we'll have to recur to here. In previous interviews, Mr. Oric has expressed some hesitancy about working with our maps, and I'm just trying to take it one step at a time with him. And may I ask the court officer to zoom out just a little bit, please, so we can see a couple of the other names. Thank you. That's perfect. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, you testified that the column of Muslim men gathered at Susnjari. Do you see that indicated on the map?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And it was your intention to head in the direction of Tuzla; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you described arriving at a hill overlooking Konjevic Polje. Can you just point out on the map -- do you see Konjevic Polje depicted on the map, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, at the time of your arrest, sir, or at the time of your capture, you were not actually in the town of Konjevic Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: This is not a town. It is a local community. We were in the centre at the crossroads towards Zvornik-Milici-Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me take you, if I can, to a couple of the -- the other landmarks on this map. Do you see Bratunac marked, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And there is a line that runs leftwards or westwards from Bratunac almost up to where Konjevic Polje is depicted; is that correct? And then the line splits to the left and to the right. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I haven't really understood. Which line?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me take you from the town of Bratunac. Do you see Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Moving leftward on the screen, do you see a road or a line passing through Glogova, then further to the left through Kravica, Sandici, and then intersecting another line or road after that? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, that -- that line or road that runs between Bratunac and that intersection at Konjevic Polje, looking at this map is that a fair representation, to your recollection, of the road that you testified before was consistently on your right as you and your various groups were making your way from Susnjari to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the road that I spoke about that was on our right side. And this is the intersection in Konjevic Polje leading to Zvornik, Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, referring specifically to that intersection you just described, if you're at the intersection and, as depicted on the map, if Konjevic Polje is to your right or, as the map depicts, slightly up, what direction does that take you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: You mean from Konjevic Polje towards Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you're standing at the intersection, that intersection of Konjevic Polje - and I'd ask you just to take a look at the map - the road goes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He answered that already, because before, line 22 and 23, he said one way takes you to Zvornik, the other one takes you to Milici. So I think he has answered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And to go to Tuzla, I think that's what you should concentrate about.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm just asking him, Your Honour, which direction would take him to Zvornik when he's standing at the intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Which direction goes to Zvornik, sir; left or right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Right. On the right-hand side. That's the direction to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, to the best that you can, can you mark on this map approximately where you believe you were arrested -- or you were captured.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: In this area, on the hill. Up on the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I would ask if --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: This is the centre. This is where I was captured and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could he put his initials against --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- taken there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- against that mark, please. Your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. For the record, the witness makes a mark -- made a mark on the map that is being used with him, starting from the red dot, which at almost 30 minutes below Konjevic Polje, perpendicularly pointing at five minutes, at the end of which he put his initials, "MO."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, if you would just write the number 1 next to that line that you drew.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show you another map. May we zoom -- is it possible to zoom out, or will we lose the focus if we ... Can you -- yes. Let me just show you the section, with the Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is a photocopy of a map, I mean, so you can barely work with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If -- Your Honour, if -- I believe he can -- he can see from the photocopy pretty well. If the focus on the screens is -- if it's just too poor for Your Honour, we can try to get a better map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's an important thing that everyone -- it's not just us, Mr. Thayer. It's everyone who is following.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Understood. I don't want to speak for anybody else, but if -- we're specifically going to be looking at Kamenica and Susnjari, and I would just ask if everybody can at least see those two locations on this map. The rest of the detail, I think, is unimportant for this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's much, much better now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if it doesn't work out, we can get a better map perhaps for tomorrow's session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now -- could we move that just a little bit up. The other way. I'm sorry. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a portion of the map on the screen, or feel free to work with the hard copy on the ELMO if you can read that better. Do you see Susnjari towards the bottom of your screen? Do you see that marked there on the map?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you move northwards slightly up and to your -- to your right -- to your left, I'm sorry, do you also see Kamenica marked?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you see slightly to the upper right and towards the top of the screen, above Kamenica, Sandici marked?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I just ask if you could underline Sandici as well, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what I'd like you to do, if you would, is write a number 1 next to Susnjari, and your initials.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And a number 2 next to Kamenica, and your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And a number 3 beside Sandici, and your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, it's slightly obscured by some of the markings on the map, but if you move to the north-east, in other words, rightwards at about 2.00, a short distance, do you see Kravica marked as well? Just above Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you please -- please underline Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now you're telepathic, sir. Moving directly below Kravica, do you see Siljkovici marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Want would you please underline, write the number 5 and your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, sir, are these the various villages that you described earlier in your testimony moving towards during your trek from Susnjari to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Kamenica was where the -- we were ambushed and where people fled. I said they were fleeing to the right towards Kravica and Siljkovici, in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. We may need to refer to these maps in the future, but I think for now that gives us a working knowledge of where we're referring to during the course of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Thayer. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we left off with you describing how prisoners were loaded onto your two buses from a meadow in the Kravica area. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were the two buses filled with prisoners at that time, with those prisoners from the meadow?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. When they filled the two buses, we headed towards Bratunac. We continued our journey.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did your bus subsequently arrive in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We arrived in Bratunac in front of the school Vuk Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were there other buses already parked there when your buses arrived?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I could see, there were two more buses there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, could you describe for the Trial Chamber, please, where the buses were parked in relation to the school.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They were parked in front of the school, in front of the entrance of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were they parked side by side or were they parked in a column or some other configuration?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They were parked one in front of the other, so one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall which number bus you were on if you're counting as number 1 the bus closest to the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I was in the third bus in this row starting from the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you able to discern, sir, whether the entrance to the school was lighted at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The street was lit by street lamps, as well as the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was your group taken off your bus?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. When the military police went off the bus, the police went. They told us to stay in the bus during the night, that there was no room in the school and that we should sit in the bus during the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let's make this clear because I definitely wouldn't like to have confusion here. He said when the military police went off the bus, and then he mentioned the police, and then "they told us." It's the same military police, I suppose, he's referring to and not another category of police.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, you testified a moment ago that the military police went off the bus and the police went and then you were told to stay on the bus during the night. First question is: Did the military police that night ever leave you unguarded on that bus?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They went off the bus, but they returned very quickly from the school, and they told us to stay on the bus. Of course, we couldn't flee from the bus because there were other soldiers around the bus, standing and guarding us. But they returned to the bus, and they told us to stay there when they came back from the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this was the same three military policemen who had been with you from the time you left Konjevic Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did they -- did the military policemen tell you who was filling up the school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't. They -- they only told us that it was full and that we couldn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber the events that occurred that night while you were parked in front of the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The first thing that happened while we were on the bus was that a soldier took me off the bus because he found an insignia, Territorial Defence of Srebrenica. He took me off the bus and he told me it belonged to me. He tried to kill me. And then the military policeman said that it did not belong to me, and that's when he put me back on the bus. As far as the subsequent events are concerned --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me stop you right there. You referred to a Territorial Defence patch. Where was this -- exactly where was this patch found, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: It was on the ground next to the bus. He had found it, and he claimed that it had belonged to me and that I threw it off the bus. That's why he tried to kill me, but fortunately he didn't, because the policeman had intervened and said that I had been searched and that it did not belong to me, and I was placed back on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you were still seated next to that window in the very back of the bus on the right-hand side; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I note from the transcript that you referred to a policeman had intervened. Are you referring to the -- one of the same three military policemen that you've been telling us about?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you had mentioned a few moments ago that the street was lit with streetlights. Can you describe whether there was a streetlight in your area at the bus?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could see everything clearly; the soldiers. The street was lit in that portion, that section. That's how he was able to see the patch lying on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: After this incident with the Territorial Defence patch ended, can you tell the Trial Chamber what you recall happening next.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Later on, while we were sitting on the bus, they told us that we couldn't fall asleep. After a while, in the front row of the seats one of the prisoners fell asleep, and one of the military policemen came in and hit him on the shoulder and said, "Why are you sleeping?" This man, as I heard from the other prisoners, hit him back. Probably he was still sleeping. He hit the policeman back, cursed at him, and said, "Look, he hit me." Then other soldiers came in from the outside, the remaining two military policemen, took this person off the bus and took him in the direction of the school, and then we heard shots. We heard a burst of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just stop you right there, sir. With respect to this prisoner who had been sleeping, did you hear any of the other prisoners on the bus say anything about that prisoner's mental state?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. People who were sitting next to him and who probably know him said that he was not entirely normal, that he was crazy. Probably because they knew him. This is what they were saying. But they took him off the bus and killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I'm looking at the transcript, sir, and the testimony indicates that you said that he hit the policeman back. And can you describe who he is? Are you talking about that man who may have had some mental problems?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes, the man who was sleeping had some mental problems and hit back the policeman, while he was still sleeping probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the transcript then says cursed at him. Who cursed at who, sir, just so the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The military policeman cursed the man, and said, "He hit me." He cursed his mother and then said, "He hit me." Then the two military policemen took him off the bus. He was holding onto the seat, so they had to literally take him off the bus. When the shot was fired, I couldn't see who had fired the shot, whether it was someone -- whether it was the soldiers or the military policemen. I heard the shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. We need to clear this, because line 2 on page 71, he -- at least, in the transcript we have, "And then we heard shots," in the plural. "We heard a burst of fire." Now, if the translation -- interpretation is correct, which I have no reason to doubt, he is referring only to one shot. So we need to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was there one shot or did you hear more than one shot fired at this man with a mental disability of some sort?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is no indication in his testimony that he saw this -- or those shots being fired at this man. He never saw the thing happening. He just testified that he heard the shots or the shot. So let's -- let us draw the conclusion, and neither you nor -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you heard the shot or shots -- I'll withdraw that question, Your Honour, and start over again. Did you hear one shot or more than one shot, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: At that moment, I heard one shot, which was actually a short burst of fire, and then I heard him scream. And in the school I could hear several shots coming from the school. When he was taken off the bus and when he was drawn towards the school, I heard a short burst of fire and then I heard him scream ever so faintly, and somebody said, "Drag him into the school."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber exactly, to the best of your recollection, what you saw occur once this man had been taken off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They were dragging him towards the school. In other words, he held onto the seat in -- in the bus. When they took him off, they dragged him towards the school. He was fighting them. Then I heard a short burst of fire, I heard him utter a faint sound, somebody said, "Drag him toward the school," and that was it. That was the end of the whole thing. If you're asking me about the night, what happened during that night on the bus --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I'll get to that in a moment. Now, you testified that this group that had taken this man off the bus had its -- their backs to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this was the three military policemen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: There were three policemen, but there were also some troops around the bus. I can't tell you who fired. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: But based on what you saw, sir, was the burst -- did the burst of fire come from somewhere within that group of soldiers and military policemen?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: During that night on the bus, was anyone beaten on your bus?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: One man was beaten. A soldier got on the bus carrying an automatic rifle with a wooden butt. He recognised a man in the front part of the bus. He started hitting him with the rifle butt, and he asked him who had killed a certain soldier, who had killed another soldier, and all the while he kept on hitting him with the rifle butt. I didn't hear any names being mentioned. I just heard him asking the man who had killed the Serbs in Jadro from an ambush. The man replied that he didn't know, and still he was hit with the rifle butt and he was kicked. And this continued until the military police returned to the bus. And then one of the military police chased the soldier out of the bus. The soldier must have been drunk. At least, that's how he appeared to me, as somebody being drunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you have any idea, based on the uniform or the clothing that this soldier wore, what military unit or detachment he was -- this soldier was serving with? Were you able to see any identifying information?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: The man who was hitting the detainee on the bus, he did not have any patches. He did not have a blouse. He had a camouflage T-shirt, and I did not see any patches on the T-shirt; no insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: During the night, sir, did anyone else board your bus and take anyone away?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of the night, another soldier got on the bus and asked if there was somebody called Catic or Dzanic on the bus. He mentioned those two family names. A person got up, went with the soldier to the school, and never returned to the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall a person named Ilija boarding the bus?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Ilija from Spat, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did this Ilija from Spat do or say when he entered your bus?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: When he got on, he asked if there was this Catic or Dzanic. He got up and went with the soldier to the school. And the man never returned to the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So it's this Ilija, in other words, who asked for this Catic or Dzanic, is that fair to say, just to be clear?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I saw Ilija -- yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, from your position in your bus, were you able to see what was going on with respect to the other buses in that column pointing towards the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I saw that all the headlights on the buses were on, and I saw the same man, Ilija from Spat, entering the other buses, whether he was there to recognise people by their names or otherwise, and he took a few people to the school and never returned them. And I saw him on several occasions bringing people from the courtyard, from the left side of the courtyard, and from there he took people into the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone other than this Ilija from Spat removing prisoners from the other buses that night?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: There was some people with him but unfamiliar to me. I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: But is it your testimony that you saw these other people whom you didn't know also removing people from the buses?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour; leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We've had a long series of leading questions, and the assumption was that, unless I hear objections from your part, we will go ahead. We have an objection now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You testified a moment ago, sir, that there were some other individuals whom you didn't know with this Ilija from Spat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were waiting in front of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did you see those individuals do that evening?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: All night through while we were there, I saw him taking people off the buses. He went to the bus that was behind us, and also from the courtyard. There is an exit from the courtyard, and he brought people from the courtyard on a couple of occasions and took them to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. My question was, though, sir, with respect to those other individuals who you stated a moment ago were with this Ilija from Spat, what do you recall seeing them doing? Not Ilija from Spat; what do you recall them doing, if anything, that night?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They waited for Ilija to bring the men and to take these men to the school, Ilija and the two other guys that were with him. The three of them took all these men to the school and never brought them back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Thayer, because sooner or later this, I think, will need to be explained. How did he know or how does he know that this man was Ilija from Spat? Did he know him from before? Has he been told that afterwards? And what ethnicity was this man, because Ilija -- the name Ilija may be misleading.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Telepathy again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This Ilija from Spat, how did you know who this individual was? Was there anything distinctive about him that you recall, and how is it that you were able to identify him?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I knew he was Ilija from Spat because I had known him before the war. He had a long moustache that he tied below his chin. I used to see him before the war in Bratunac and in Srebrenica. So he did have a distinctive feature; the moustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is Spat, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Spat is a village close to Sase where the Sase mine is. It is all in Srebrenica municipality. Spat, in other words, is a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how close is Spat to the -- the town of Bratunac, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Maybe a dozen kilometres or so, 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the ethnicity of this person?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know what the ethnicity of this Ilija from Spat was, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Yes. He is a Serb, of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps another matter that he could address, because again it will arise sooner or later: I mean, he recognised Ilija from Spat, but did Ilija from Spat who was going on the bus, looking for individuals there, ever recognise him if he knew him from before?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you understand the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was very young then. I knew him personally because I saw him around Bratunac. And when I explained to some people that I had seen this man from the long moustache, they told me that was Ilija from Spat. Before that, I used to see him around Bratunac, but whether he recognised me or not, I don't know. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified that during the course of the night you saw men being removed from the buses and taken to the school. Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber the sequence of events that you would see and hear when you saw someone being taken off the buses.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: They got on the buses. They took people. They took them to the school. And then in the school during the night I heard screams and wailing. Not from everybody but from some individuals. And we could also hear bursts of fire, even some bursts of fire in the school, coming from the school. And this lasted all night long.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when prisoners were brought inside the school, would you hear screaming coming right away, or would there be some time that would pass before you heard the screaming, or was it a mixture of the two during the course of the night?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: Once they left, after a certain time we would hear screams and bursts of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any of the prisoners returned to the bus that night, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How about the other buses, sir, not just the one that you were on?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: I did not see anybody return or being returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you given any food or water that night, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN ORIC
utterances.text: We got water but no food.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note that it's about 12.35. I have a sketch -- I'm sorry, it's 1.35. I beg your pardon. I have a sketch which I'm prepared to work with Mr. Oric through. In an abundance of caution, I think it may be a better idea to wait until tomorrow when he's a little fresher to go through another e-court exhibit and explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's no problem on our part. So we will adjourn for today. So more or less it's now -- all right. Mr. Oric, we are going to stop here for today. We will resume with your testimony tomorrow afternoon, 2.15. Use the time that you have to relax, because we've got a long session tomorrow, longer than today. And we will start with the cross-examination, I suppose, one of the cross-examinations tomorrow. In the meantime, it's important that you do not communicate with anyone on the events that you're giving evidence about, or let anyone try to communicate with you. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
